name: Gantry Plaza
subtitle: The city, seen from the water.
access: Use the designated fishing pier. Follow current park signs and avoid ferry operations. The pin marks the park vicinity, not a guaranteed open casting position.
why: A designated pier makes this a useful starting point for an East River shore trip. Coastal species below are regional possibilities, not a site-specific catch report.

name: Prospect Park Lake
subtitle: A freshwater chapter in Brooklyn.
access: Fish from permitted shoreline areas; respect fences and refuge signs. Catch and release, barbless hooks and non-lead weights.
why: A practical lake choice for a light tackle outing. DEC documents bass and sunfish here; vegetation favors weedless presentations.

name: Pier 34
subtitle: Two fingers reaching into the Hudson.
access: Use the public southern finger. The northern finger belongs to tunnel operations and is closed to the public. Follow posted fishing restrictions.
why: The park identifies the southern finger as a fishing place. A clear choice for a Manhattan estuary visit; regional species are possibilities, not predictions.

name: Van Cortlandt Lake
subtitle: A quiet edge below the woods.
access: Shoreline includes grassy and steeper wooded areas. Choose a stable, permitted place to stand; the 1 train reaches 242nd Street nearby.
why: DEC records a diverse warmwater community. Suits a patient bass or panfish session with light tackle.

name: Kissena Lake
subtitle: Small water. Plenty to observe.
access: Public shoreline in Kissena Park. Avoid discolored water or visible algal blooms and follow closures. Catch and release only.
why: A compact lake for a simple float rig. DEC’s 2022 survey documented bass, sunfish, bullhead and crappie; it is historical evidence.

name: Clove Lake
subtitle: An island lake beneath the trees.
access: Choose permitted shoreline at Clove Lakes Park. Respect other park users, posted access and vegetated edges.
why: A Staten Island freshwater option with bass and panfish listed by DEC. Bring a small float rig and a landing net.

name: Steeplechase Pier
subtitle: Where the boardwalk meets the Atlantic.
access: The fishing pier is off the boardwalk near West 19th Street. Exposed conditions can change quickly; check signs and keep clear of waves.
why: A designated shore-fishing destination on DEC’s NYC map. Suits an open-coast outing with saltwater gear; species are regional possibilities.
